target: Eu não sabia nadar quando era pequeno.
english: I didn't know how to swim when I was young.
old: Imperfeito of 'saber': sabia (eu). 'Saber' in imperfeito = used to know / didn't know (ongoing state).
focus: sabia = knew (ongoing) vs soube = found out – lead with the meaning contrast, cut the 'Imperfeito of saber' label lead

target: Eu fiz uma besteira enorme.
english: I made a huge mistake.
old: 'Fazer' past: eu fiz. 'Fazer besteira' = to do something stupid/make a blunder.
focus: fazer besteira = to do something dumb (besteira from 'besta', beast) – drop the 'Fazer past' conjugation lead

target: Eu disse que não podia ir.
english: I said I couldn't go.
old: 'Dizer' in the past: disse, disse, dissemos, disseram. The eu and ele/ela forms are the same: 'eu disse' = 'ele disse.'
focus: disse = both 'I said' AND 'he/she said' – only the pronoun tells; drop the four-form paradigm

target: Vocês foram felizes nessa decisão.
english: You were happy with that decision.
old: 'Ser/Ir' past: vocês foram. Here 'foram felizes' = were happy, so it's past of 'ser.'
focus: foram = both 'went' and 'were'; 'foram felizes' shows the adjective complement signals ser here – lead with the ambiguity

target: Vocês disseram algo para ele?
english: Did you say anything to him?
old: Plural: `vocês` is universal. Portugal also has `vós` but it's extinct in speech. Just use `vocês` and you're safe everywhere.
focus: vocês is the universal plural you – vós exists on paper in Portugal but is extinct in speech; strip backticks

target: Vocês viram aquele programa na TV?
english: Did you see that TV show?
old: 'Ver' past: vocês viram. Don't confuse 'viram' (saw) with 'vieram' (came). 'Aquele programa' = that show.
focus: viram (saw) vs vieram (came) – one letter apart; drop the conj lead and the 'aquele programa' gloss

target: Ela disse que vai pensar no assunto.
english: She said she'll think about it.
old: 'Dizer' past: ela disse. 'Disse que vai' – the reported speech keeps the original tense in casual Brazilian Portuguese.
focus: Portuguese reported speech keeps the original tense: disse que vai = said she WILL (English backshifts to 'would') – drop the conj lead

target: Eu vi um acidente na estrada.
english: I saw an accident on the road.
old: 'Ver' in the past: vi, viu, vimos, viram. Very short forms – don't confuse 'vi' (I saw) with 'vim' (I came).
focus: vi (I saw) vs vim (I came) – one letter; drop the four-form paradigm, anchor on 'vi um acidente'

target: Ele pôs as chaves na mesa.
english: He put the keys on the table.
old: 'Pôr' in the past: pus, pôs, pusemos, puseram. In casual speech, many Brazilians say 'coloquei' instead of 'pus.'
focus: in casual speech Brazilians say colocar, not pôr ('coloquei' for 'pus') – anchor on 'pôs as chaves', drop the paradigm

target: A gente brincava de esconde-esconde.
english: We used to play hide and seek.
old: Imperfeito of -ar: brincava (a gente). 'Brincar de' + game = to play (a game). 'Esconde-esconde' = hide and seek.
focus: brincar DE + game – Portuguese plays 'of' a game; cut the conjugation line and the esconde-esconde gloss

target: Eu sonhava em morar no exterior.
english: I used to dream of living abroad.
old: Imperfeito of -ar: sonhava (eu). 'Sonhar em' = to dream of. Describes an ongoing past aspiration.
focus: sonhar EM, not 'de' – English 'dream of' misleads; anchor on 'sonhava em morar', drop the conjugation line

target: Ele me indicou um bom restaurante.
english: He suggested a good restaurant.
old: 'Me' as indirect: 'me indicou' = recommended to me. 'Indicar' = to recommend/suggest.
focus: indicar looks like 'indicate' but means recommend/suggest – anchor on 'me indicou um bom restaurante'

target: Ele trabalhava num banco antes de mudar de área.
english: He used to work at a bank before switching fields.
old: Imperfeito of -ar: trabalhava (ele). 'Antes de' + infinitive = before doing something.
focus: antes de + infinitive where English uses -ing ('antes de mudar' = before switching); drop the conjugation line

target: Sem que ninguém perceba, ele saiu.
english: Without anyone noticing, he left.
old: 'Sem que' always requires the subjunctive.
focus: correct but bare 41 chars – add the card's own example: 'sem que ninguém perceba' (perceba is the subjunctive)

target: Não há ninguém que saiba disso.
english: There's no one who knows about this.
old: Subjunctive is used after indefinite/negative antecedents.
focus: no-one-who-exists takes subjunctive – say it in plain words and quote 'ninguém que saiba'; kill 'indefinite/negative antecedents' jargon

target: Eu fiz isso para ajudar você.
english: I did this to help you.
old: 'Para' expresses purpose – wHY you do something. 'Para ajudar' = in order to help. Think of 'para' as 'for the purpose of.'
focus: para + infinitive = purpose is right – fix the 'wHY' typo and tighten; keep the 'para ajudar' anchor

target: Ela se maquiou rapidinho antes de sair.
english: She put on makeup quickly before leaving.
old: 'Se maquiar' = to put on makeup. 'Rapidinho' = really quickly – diminutive of 'rápido' used as adverb.
focus: one rule only: 'rapidinho' – diminutive of rápido working as an adverb; drop the se-maquiar gloss

target: Para onde vocês vão nas férias?
english: Where are you going on vacation?
old: 'Para onde' = to where (destination with purpose). Used when asking about travel destinations.
focus: Motion needs 'para onde' (or aonde) – bare 'onde' asks location only; English drops the 'to'.

target: Eu vou ligar para você mais tarde.
english: I'll call you later.
old: In spoken Brazilian Portuguese, 'ir + infinitive' is far more common than the simple future (falarei).
focus: Quote 'vou ligar' – spoken BP uses ir + infinitive; simple future 'ligarei' sounds stiff and written.

target: A gente os encontrou na praia.
english: We found them at the beach.
old: 'Os' is the masculine plural direct object pronoun (them). 'As' is the feminine plural. In casual speech, 'eles/elas' is more common.
focus: Spoken BP would say 'encontrou eles' – the clitic 'os' reads formal/written; make that contrast the hook.

target: Não acho que ele venha hoje.
english: I don't think he's coming today.
old: Negative opinion ('não acho que') triggers subjunctive.
focus: 'Acho que' takes indicative, but negated 'não acho que' flips to subjunctive 'venha' – the flip is the hook.

target: É estranho que ele não tenha ligado.
english: It's strange that he hasn't called.
old: 'É estranho que' expresses emotion, triggering subjunctive.
focus: After 'é estranho que' even a real event takes subjunctive – 'tenha ligado'; emotion, not doubt, triggers it.

target: Eu lhe garanto que vai dar certo.
english: I guarantee you it will work out.
old: 'Lhe' = to you (formal indirect). 'Garantir' = to guarantee/assure. 'Que vai dar certo' = that it will work out.
focus: One rule only: 'lhe' here = 'to you' (pairs with você), not 'to him' – cut the garantir/dar-certo glosses.

target: Olha só que legal!
english: Look how cool!
old: 'Olha só' is an informal expression used to draw attention.
focus: 'Só' here isn't 'only' – 'olha só' = 'just look', an attention-grabber; the só landmine is the hook.

target: Confirme sua reserva com antecedência.
english: Confirm your reservation in advance.
old: Formal imperatives use the subjunctive: 'Faça o favor' (Please do), 'Sente-se' (Sit down) – used with 'o senhor/a senhora'.
focus: Quote 'Confirme' – formal commands use the subjunctive form; the informal command would be 'confirma'.

target: Os amigos com quem saí ontem são do trabalho.
english: The friends I went out with yesterday are from work.
old: 'com quem' – preposition + 'quem' for people in relative clauses. The preposition must come before the relative pronoun.
focus: English strands the preposition ('friends I went out with'); Portuguese must front it – 'com quem saí'.

target: Não toque nisso!
english: Don't touch that!
old: Negative commands always use the subjunctive form, even informally.
focus: Quote 'não toque' – positive informal command is 'toca', but negation flips to the subjunctive form 'toque'.

target: Eu pagarei quando receber o salário.
english: I'll pay when I get my salary.
old: The simple future (falarei, falará) sounds formal in Brazilian Portuguese – reserved for writing and formal speech.
focus: Anchor on 'pagarei' – the simple future reads formal/written in BP; speech would say 'vou pagar'.

target: O livro que eu comprei é muito bom.
english: The book I bought is very good.
old: 'Que' is the most common relative pronoun in Brazilian Portuguese, used for both people and things.
focus: Real trap: English drops the relative ('the book I bought') but Portuguese must keep que – 'o livro que eu comprei'.

target: A razão pela qual ele faltou é desconhecida.
english: The reason why he was absent is unknown.
old: 'Pelo qual/pela qual' – 'por + o qual' contracts.
focus: 'pela qual' = por + a qual, literally 'by which' – how Portuguese says 'the reason why'; add a hook and quote the card's phrase.

target: Haverá uma festa de confraternização na empresa.
english: There will be a company party.
old: 'Haverá' is the future of 'haver' – used formally for 'there will be'.
focus: 'Haverá' is formal 'there will be' – contrast with everyday speech 'vai ter uma festa'.

target: Se eu soubesse cozinhar como ela, abriria um restaurante.
english: If I could cook like her, I'd open a restaurant.
old: 'Se pudesse' introduces a hypothetical ability – paired with the conditional for the imagined result.
focus: Tip cites 'pudesse' but the card has 'soubesse' – English 'could cook' uses saber (know-how), not poder; quote 'se eu soubesse cozinhar'.

target: Come-se bem neste restaurante.
english: One eats well at this restaurant.
old: Impersonal 'se' – no specific subject, describes general experience.
focus: 'Come-se bem' = 'one eats well' – se makes the verb subjectless like English 'one/you'; quote the card's come-se.

target: Quem não tem cão, caça com gato.
english: Whoever doesn't have a dog, hunts with a cat.
old: Popular Brazilian saying meaning you make do with what you have.
focus: Quote the card ('caça com gato') and keep the meaning gloss – you make do with what you have.

target: Nós tínhamos ouvido boatos sobre a empresa.
english: We had heard rumors about the company.
old: Portuguese uses 'ter' (not 'haver') for compound tenses: 'tinha feito' = had done. Past participles never change form.
focus: One rule only: compound past uses ter – anchor on 'tínhamos ouvido' = we had heard; cut the second rule about participle agreement.

target: Se eu soubesse que você estava aqui, teria vindo antes.
english: If I had known you were here, I would have come earlier.
old: 'Se soubesse' (if I knew/had known) – 'saber' in the imperfect subjunctive for hypothetical knowledge.
focus: 'Se soubesse' covers both 'if I knew' and 'if I had known' – drop the jargon lead, keep the two-way English mapping.

target: Aqui se fala português.
english: Portuguese is spoken here.
old: 'Se' + verb in 3rd person creates a passive/impersonal construction.
focus: 'Se fala' = 'is spoken' – se turns the verb passive with no 'is'; anchor on the card's 'aqui se fala'.

target: O médico recomendou que ele tomasse mais água.
english: The doctor recommended he drink more water.
old: Verbs of recommendation/suggestion in reported speech use the subjunctive: 'recomendou que fizesse'.
focus: Use THIS card's clause – 'recomendou que tomasse': recommendation verbs force the past subjunctive where English just says 'he drink'.

target: O pai disse ao filho que precisava estudar mais.
english: The father told his son he needed to study more.
old: 'Falar que' is more informal than 'dizer que' for reported speech – very common in Brazilian Portuguese.
focus: Anchor on the card's 'disse que' – standard reported speech; casual BP speech swaps in 'falou que'.

target: Uma vez que a decisão foi tomada, não há como voltar atrás.
english: Once the decision has been made, there's no going back.
old: 'Uma vez que' means 'since/given that'.
focus: Landmine: looks like 'one time that' but uma vez que = 'once/given that' - causal-temporal, not counting times.

target: À medida que envelhecemos, ficamos mais sábios.
english: As we age, we become wiser.
old: 'À medida que' means 'as/to the extent that' – indicates parallel progression.
focus: English 'as' trap: a medida que is the proportional 'as' (the more X, the more Y), not 'como'.

target: Ou seja, a reunião foi cancelada.
english: In other words, the meeting was canceled.
old: 'Ou seja' = 'in other words/that is'.
focus: Literal hook: ou seja = 'or be it' (seja is subjunctive of ser), frozen into 'in other words'.

target: Ela costuma acordar cedo durante a semana.
english: She usually wakes up early during the week.
old: 'Costumar' + infinitive = to usually do something – habitual action.
focus: English packs the habit into the adverb 'usually'; Portuguese uses a verb: costuma acordar = 'is in the habit of waking'.

target: Ele volta e meia esquece as chaves.
english: He keeps forgetting his keys.
old: 'Volta e meia' = every now and then/keeps on.
focus: Literal hook: volta e meia = 'a turn and a half' - every so often.

target: Ela é muito gata, todo mundo concorda.
english: She's really hot, everyone agrees.
old: 'Gato/gata' = hot/attractive person – common Brazilian slang.
focus: Landmine: gata is literally 'cat' - calling someone a cat means they're hot.

target: Que ele faça o que quiser.
english: Let him do whatever he wants.
old: Subjunctive used in the third person to express 'let him/her'.
focus: Quote the card ('Que ele faca'): que + subjunctive opens a wish/command = 'let him', with no word for 'let'.
